## Introduction

In this seven-minute demonstration, we store versions of the
documented dataset and retrieve a pipeline-produced model by its
identifier. By the end, you should be able to explain how a version
identifier links a result to the exact input that produced it.

The pipeline in the hands-on activities reads a pinned dataset
version, so you prepared the board before the session. The instructor
runs the code below from the project root; the board and identifiers
in your MyBinder session are your own.
[Prepare the dataset versions](00_preparation.qmd#preparation-versions)

## Store dataset versions with pins

Allow about four minutes. A *pins* board stores named objects, called
pins. We use a local folder board with versioning enabled explicitly,
so writing changed data adds a version and keeps the previous one.
An identical write is skipped by default. We store the data as RDS,
an R format that preserves the column types.

The prepared script writes two versions of the `health_wellbeing` pin.
The first contains all 29 studies, with the source URL and raw-file
checksum as metadata. The second contains the 18 general-population
studies. It is read from the exact full version, and its metadata
records the filter and that parent version. Rerunning the script
reuses identical versions instead of writing duplicates.

We open the same board and list its versions.

```{r health-versioning-board, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
box::use(
  pins[board_folder, pin_exists, pin_meta, pin_read, pin_versions],
  utils[read.csv]
)

source("pipelines/workshop_support.R")
workshop_dir <- workshop_output_dir()
data_board <- board_folder(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "data_store"),
  versioned = TRUE
)
pin_versions(data_board, "health_wellbeing")
```

The script also recorded which identifier belongs to which dataset.
We retrieve the subset's metadata and the full dataset by those
identifiers.

```{r health-versioning-read, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
versions <- read.csv(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "dataset-versions.csv"),
  colClasses = "character"
)
full_version <- versions$version[versions$scope == "all"]
general_version <- versions$version[versions$scope == "general"]
stopifnot(length(full_version) == 1L, length(general_version) == 1L)

pin_meta(data_board, "health_wellbeing", version = general_version)$user

health_full <- pin_read(
  data_board, "health_wellbeing", version = full_version
)
nrow(health_full)
```

A version identifier names a stored object within this board. If you
recreate the board elsewhere, it receives new identifiers, so retain
the upstream checksum and the filter as well. In the hands-on
activities, the pipeline reads the version named in
`analysis-data-version.txt` rather than whichever version is newest.

## Store model versions with vetiver

Allow about three minutes. The reference pipeline uses the checked study
summaries in two branches. One fits the random-effects meta-analysis. The
other trains a small illustrative regression of Fisher z on log sample
size, then stores it with *vetiver*. The regression and the pooled estimate
answer different questions.

This is a preview of one pipeline output. Before the session, the
instructor ran the workshop pipeline's model branch on the full dataset
and saved the model pin. The next lesson shows where that branch fits
in the pipeline. If you are trying this demo on your own, first run
`source("pipelines/prepare_versioning_demo.R")` from the project root.

Read the saved version identifier and use it to retrieve the model.
Its input prototype lists the columns required for prediction. Its
metadata records the training data version and checksum. When you
run the completed pipeline against the same input on this board,
its summary records the same model version.

```{r health-vetiver-read, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
version_file <- file.path(workshop_dir, "predictive-model-version.txt")
model_version <- readLines(version_file, warn = FALSE)
model_version
model_board <- pins::board_folder(file.path(workshop_dir, "model_store"), versioned = TRUE)
model <- vetiver::vetiver_pin_read(
  model_board, "health_wellbeing_lm", version = model_version
)
names(model$prototype)
model$metadata$user[c("data_version", "data_file_md5")]
```

The training version should match the full dataset identifier you read
above. Changing the dataset in the pipeline also trains and pins
a new model. The [optional input comparison](07_modify_and_reproduce.qmd#change-input)
lets you see both versions. Review sharing terms for any fitted model,
especially when it was trained on restricted data [@vetiver-pin-write].

## Checkpoint {#versioning-checkpoint}

- The data board lists two versions of `health_wellbeing`. The full
  version returns 29 rows, and the subset's metadata records its
  filter and parent version.
- The stored model expects `log_n` and records the training dataset version
  and checksum.
- You can explain why the pipeline reads a named version rather than
  the newest one.
